body:
For that we need to plan issues to ensure we fully support the highest possible quality of sound simulation

If that is performance that blocks us, we should add sound simulation in Rust background worker and make it default, and organize streaming with variable quality, so as soon as we detect that our algorithm is too slow for the device we make quality less expensive in computation.

Also we can do some background checks without playing sounds when page loaded, without locking the UI. So we do small benchmark to understand actual performance of the device, and adjust our precision to it.

We should double check we have much more configuration for the voice simulation.

So the voice is highly realistic as possible.

We should also use our own simulation to be able to be running in reverse, so we can use not only do text to speech, but also speech to text.

We always to text in language -> IPA -> audio, and back audio -> IPA -> detected language or mix of languages.

We also should use datasets of real voice recording (preferably public domain recordings with prepared transcripts so it is easier for us), so we can recognize it using our algorithms (simulation in reverse) and also be able to reproduce it.

We can use multi pass algorithm that will first try to fit best simulation settings to copy the voice, after that it should be able to reverse simulation perfectly matching detected voice configuration and once stabilized we can just have both configuration of voice recognition, so we can copy voice, but as person continue speaking we should also be able to precisely recognize what he/she is talking about.

In both speaking we highlight each syllable, and in recognition also we highlight each syllable as recognition goes.

As tests may be computationally expensive we should use manually triggered GitHub Actions to make it work.

We should target for algorithm to be fast in CPUs (if possible use multicore CPUs), but it also should work just fine with single CPU.

And everything should work perfectly with lowest possible audio settings (synthesis, recognition, copy/configuration detection and so on).

We should check all best practices in the industry/internet/online on github and so on, we should list all similar projects or projects that has implemented parts of our vision.

Our vision must be updated as the result of this pull request.

We also need to plan issues in this repository, so they so detailed, so even not smart AI agent can deliver it perfectly. All issues should be marked as bugs/features, and also clearly marked blockers should be between them, so we have full development plan for all described issues here, and all requirements you recommended to achieve our previous vision and new vision.

We also should invest carefully in different linguistic ideas, like tones, accents, increasing or decreasing volume, question/exclamation intonations, whisper, conveying emotions and so on.

So all modes of speech which is commonly used are covered both for input and output of our system.

We should not use neural networks, just algorithms, pure math, physically accurate simulations and reverse simulations and so on.

We must do new state of the art system, which never existed before and gift it to the humanity as public domain project.

So the scope of this issue is docs update, and as the result we should get actually created issues on GitHub with a full plan we will implement step by step.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
